relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan and the most directly comparable prior art in the slice for the folio's q-deformed hadron programme. It asks whether SU(2) isospin is really a quantum group, builds pion, nucleon and Delta wavefunctions from a q-quark doublet, redoes the quark-model magnetic moments and mass relations — and reports a specific NEGATIVE: a single q of U_q(sl(2)) cannot parametrize the charged-neutral pion mass difference without explicit electromagnetic corrections, stated in the abstract as 'it is not true that the extra parameter q allows one to fit anything'. That matters here because rem:meson-mass-splitting asserts that q-deformation lifts the meson octet degeneracy through quantum dimensions, crossing energy and Markov-trace weights, and the folio has a live pion prediction path (computations/probes/m_pi_hecke_prediction_probe.py, computations/gmo_meson_crosscheck.py). The folio also maintains rem:q-deformed-nuclear-models-comparison, a block whose explicit job is comparing against q-deformed models, which does not mention this line of work. Supporting rather than core: it supplies a caution and a falsifiable target, not a result the folio derives from. Scoping note per the refuted-claims rule: the negative here is scope-(a) — a single-q U_q(sl(2)) isospin deformation, as tested in that paper, did not reproduce the charged-neutral pion splitting. It is not a claim that q-deformation is excluded from meson mass splittings, and the folio's mechanism (Hecke Markov trace on knot representatives) is not the same construction.

keyResults.statement: Baryon magnetic moments and mass relations go through smoothly under a q-deformed isospin doublet, but the charged-neutral pion mass difference cannot be parametrized by the single quantum-group parameter q without invoking explicit electromagnetic corrections.
keyResults.useForFolio: A falsifiable benchmark for rem:meson-mass-splitting: if the folio's q-deformed splitting mechanism is genuinely different from a single-q isospin deformation, it should be able to say what it predicts for the charged-neutral pion splitting where that route failed.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; this is prior art on exactly the question rem:meson-mass-splitting addresses, and rem:q-deformed-nuclear-models-comparison exists precisely to survey q-deformed models.

Run the folio's own meson machinery against the charged-neutral pion splitting that defeated the single-q route, and record the result whichever way it comes out. This is a cross-check of a published negative, not an import of any number from it.
